rubric.result: The objective promises two things: the page can read gate 1's state, and it can press the freeze with the key it was handed. Both are in the diff and both were checked against what the endpoint actually answers, not against the brief alone. GET: spec-freeze-route.ts sends {"status":"none"}, {"status":"no-spec"}, {status:'draft',spec,findings:[{code,line,detail}],key?} with the key omitted (never null) when it was not minted, and {status:'frozen',spec,on,pullRequest} with pullRequest nullable; client.ts's toOutcome parses exactly those four and nothing else, maps an absent key to null and a nullable pullRequest to null, so no shape the route sends is missed and no shape it never sends is parsed. POST: the route reads request.get(GateKey.HEADER) with GateKey.HEADER = 'x-gate-key', is wired in api-server.ts with no JsonBody.demandDeclared and no body reader, answers 200 {status:'frozen',on,pullRequest} on success and {code,detail} at 403/400 otherwise; freeze() posts with that header, no body and no Content-Type, reads 200 as frozen and any other status carrying {code,detail} as refused. Two real-world notes that are not this diff's defects: (a) a spec whose state line says CONGELADA but whose date line is missing or '—' makes frozenOn() null, and the route then sends on:null, which this client reads as unavailable — it cannot do otherwise, because the brief's Contract block declares frozen's on as a non-nullable string; (b) a browser sends no Origin header on a same-origin GET, so GateKey.forThePage returns null and the real page will read key:null on every draft, leaving the press unpressable. That hole lives in gate-key.ts/spec-freeze-route.ts from tasks 8-9, outside this task's **Files:**, and the brief explicitly orders this client to read a keyless draft as key:null, so it is reported here as an observation for a person and not as a finding against this diff.

The **TDD:** line names it('reads a draft with its key and every finding the backend named') and fixes the assertion: SpecFreezeMother.draftWithMarker() becomes kind:'draft' with the finding's code, line and detail untouched and the key it carried. client.test.ts:9 carries that test verbatim and asserts toEqual({kind:'draft', spec: SpecFreezeMother.SPEC, findings:[SpecFreezeMother.MARKER_FINDING, SpecFreezeMother.HYPOTHESIS_FINDING], key: SpecFreezeMother.KEY}) — same input (the mother's draftWithMarker body), same expected value, and the two findings it names carry line 42/detail and line null/detail null, so code, line and detail are all pinned untouched, including the null pair. Its boundary pair is there too: 'reads a draft with no key as key null instead of unavailable' asserts key: null over draftWithoutKey(), which is exactly what the TDD line demands of it.

Both Contract blocks are stated name by name. SpecFreeze.types.ts declares FreezeFinding {code: string; line: number | null; detail: string | null}, PullRequestRef {number: number; url: string}, the five-member SpecFreezeOutcome and the three-member FreezeAskOutcome, identical to the brief down to field names, order and nullability. client.ts exports SpecFreezeClient with read(): Promise<SpecFreezeOutcome> and freeze(key: string): Promise<FreezeAskOutcome>, the two names and shapes the second block fixes. The prose constants hold too: PATH = '/spec-freeze' (once, which is what the grep control pins), the header literal 'x-gate-key' matching GateKey.HEADER, POST with no body, non-200 with {code,detail} read as refused with error carrying detail, a throwing fetch read as unavailable on the read and backend-unreachable on the press, a draft with no key field read as key:null, POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 2000, the stop on frozen, and SpecFreezeMother carrying all eight scenario names the brief lists.

Four rows bear on this diff and each is implemented with the value the table states. D-22 (gates are the human's, triggered only from the front, an attempt without the key refused with an explicit code): the press is a function the page calls with the key it was handed in the header, and the refusal codes come back as data through kind:'refused' with code and detail. D-6 (gate 1 is an act of the app, a button the program answers for): the client exposes read/freeze for a button, and writes nothing into any document itself. D-23 (the press answers the freeze date and the pull request): FreezeAskOutcome's frozen carries on and pullRequest, and the client requires both before calling it frozen. D-7 (no merge button anywhere, the app never writes to a pull request): the client has exactly two calls, a GET and the freeze POST, and no path towards a merge or any pull-request write. No other row is touched: nothing here names cmux, stores a phase, reimplements a yardstick or pastes plugin context into a prompt.

Exemplars: client.ts is the shape of app/coordinating-session/client.ts line for line (PATH constant, isRecord predicate, a toOutcome that falls back to the unavailable member, read() wrapped whole in try/catch, freeze() with only the fetch inside the try and the {code,detail} projection after it); useSpecFreeze.ts is useCoordinatingSession.ts with one added line, the return on frozen the brief asks for; SpecFreezeMother.ts is CoordinatingSessionMother.ts's shape (literal wire bodies plus the constants the assertions reuse); the two test files mirror the exemplar tests, fake timers included. conventions/defects.md, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — SpecFreezeOutcome and FreezeAskOutcome are discriminated unions whose absent/failed states ('none', 'unavailable', 'backend-unreachable') are members rather than optionals, and no boolean stands in for any of them; the one loose string left is FreezeFinding.code, which the backend holds as the closed FreezeFindingCode, but the brief's Contract block declares it `code: string` verbatim and item 3 measures that block literally, so the diff cannot satisfy both — declared here and left out of the findings, and nothing in this diff dispatches over that code; (2) raw map as the return value of logic — none: the only map read by key is the unknown wire body inside toOutcome/freeze, which is the serialization boundary itself, and what leaves is always a typed member of the union; (3) two fields that have to agree / sentinel — none: key, line, detail and pullRequest all carry their absence as null in the type, no empty string or zero stands for an absence, and phase/kind in SpecFreezeRead are the exemplar's connecting-vs-read pair, not two fields that must agree; (4) errors named for what happens — no error type is introduced, and the three failure members ('unavailable', 'refused', 'backend-unreachable') name what happened rather than where. conventions/boundaries.md: what comes from outside is validated on entry with predicates and no cast, only the keys consumed are projected, and the backend's failure arrives as data (a status and a body) instead of a throw. conventions/testing.md: the objects come from a mother with named scenarios, the assertions are on the literal wire payload and on what the client returned, and the arrange is not built with the piece under test. conventions/style.md: no prose, English throughout, no default export, no climbing import — but the new modules put their helpers at module level, which is the one finding below. Two more things declared rather than reported: the press test feeds SpecFreezeMother.frozen(), the GET body, to a POST whose real answer carries no `spec` key — the brief fixed the eight scenario names and none of them is a POST body, and the fields the test asserts (on, pullRequest) are exactly the ones the route sends; and conventions/decisions.md's rule for the two halves of a cross-process contract would want a test comparing this wire vocabulary with the backend's, which this task's **Files:** has no room for and which no other client in this repository has either.

Does not apply: the diff is 310 insertions and 0 deletions across six files that are all new (mode 100644, index 0000000), so there is no `-` line anywhere and no pre-existing test, case or assertion could have been removed, relaxed or rewritten.

The behaviour the objective promises is produced by production code. The parse of the four states, the key-to-null rule and the unavailable fallback live in client.ts's toOutcome; the header, the bodyless POST and the refused/backend-unreachable projection live in client.ts's freeze; the two-second cadence and the stop on frozen live in useSpecFreeze.ts's effect. The test's own scaffolding is the mother's literal wire bodies and the stubbed global fetch, which is the boundary being cut, not the behaviour: revert any of those production lines and the matching test falls — remove `if (outcome.kind === 'frozen') return` and the hook test sees two calls instead of one; remove the try/catch in read() and the unreachable test rejects instead of returning unavailable. No expected value is hard-coded in a way that survives the production code being taken out.

Every line inside the six declared files traces to a sentence of the task. The two Contract blocks account for SpecFreeze.types.ts and client.ts; the prose paragraph accounts for the path, the header, the bodyless POST, the key-to-null rule, POLL_INTERVAL_MS and the stop on frozen; the **Tests:** list accounts for the five client tests and the one hook test. The eight mother scenarios are named one by one by the task itself ('SpecFreezeMother gives the scenarios by name: none, noSpec, draftWithMarker, draftReady, draftWithoutKey, frozen, notFreezable, notFromThePage'), so the four that no test in this task calls — none, noSpec, draftReady, notFromThePage, not the two the report declares — are asked for by the task's own text and are the panel's scenarios for task 12, with the burden declared in the report exactly as conventions/simplicity.md prescribes when it cannot be discharged today; that is right, not dead weight. Nothing named in ### Out of scope is touched: no groom, no slices table, no plugin skill, no merge path, no change to start-plan, implement-plan or the dispatcher. The only symbol beyond the blocks is the SpecFreezeRead type the hook returns, which the exemplar exports the same way and which the hook cannot do without. The diff carries no hunk of the plan file, so there is no amendment to rule on.

Six new tests, all three properties held. Deterministic: no real clock (the mother's ON is the literal '2026-09-14', never today's date), no network (fetch is stubbed globally), no randomness, no sleep — the cadence is driven by vi.useFakeTimers() and advanceTimersByTimeAsync(2000). Isolated: client.test.ts unstubs globals after each test, useSpecFreeze.test.ts unstubs and restores real timers, each test builds its own stub and the file needs no order; no fixed file, port or directory is taken for granted. Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on what SpecFreezeClient or the hook returned or on the literal request the client sent ('/spec-freeze' with method POST and the x-gate-key header), never on a mock's call count standing in for behaviour — the one call-count assertion, toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) after advancing two seconds, is the observable effect of the production line that stops the poll, and it goes to two the moment that line is reverted. Loaded control-tower-loop:test-driven-development for the finer half: its 'One thing. "and" in name? Split it.' would bite on 'the press sends the key in its header and reads the pull request back' and on the unreachable test asserting both read and press, but both names and that pairing are written into the brief's **Tests:** list, so the implementer answers for neither and they stay out of the findings.

findings.what: client.ts is a module born today and puts six helpers at module level (isRecord, isPullRequestRef, isNullablePullRequestRef, isFreezeFinding, isFreezeFindings, toOutcome) instead of hanging them off a type. conventions/style.md grants its declared-debt exemption only to 'a module that was already there' and closes the hole in the same breath — 'a new concept is a new module and is born conforming' — and per item 5 the written rule beats the exemplar, so app/coordinating-session/client.ts having the same shape does not settle it. Scoped deliberately: the two public entrypoints do hang off SpecFreezeClient, and their shape was fixed by the brief's Contract block ('export const SpecFreezeClient: { read(): ...; freeze(key: string): ... }'), as was useSpecFreeze's, so neither of those is counted here. It costs nothing and changes nothing — style only, and the repository's own frontend yardstick (frontend/__tests__/yardstick.test.ts) does not measure it.
findings.evidence: conventions/style.md: 'No free function at module level: every function hangs off a type. Method, class method or static method, the entrypoint included.' — against `const isRecord = (value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> =>` at the head of a new module.
